units.tr: In a simple syllogism, the whole consequent part of the question is set out in the proposition, and the antecedent part in the assumption.

units.la: 333 Modi Syllogismi simplicis melius explicantur per quantitatem & qualitatem axiomatum, quam per illa vocabula Barbara Celarent, &c.
units.tr: The modes of the simple syllogism are better explained by the quantity and quality of the axioms than by those words Barbara, Celarent, etc.

units.la: 334 Omnis Syllogismus simplex, si sit legitimus, est in aliqua trium figurarum vel specierum.
units.tr: Every simple syllogism, if it is legitimate, is in one of the three figures or species.

units.la: 335 Tot sunt figuræ quot sunt dispositiones tertii argumenti, ad necessariò concludendum.
units.tr: There are as many figures as there are arrangements of the middle term that yield a necessary conclusion.

units.la: 336 Illa dispositionis forma est vera quæ in qualibet materia suppositis præmissis necessariò concludit.
units.tr: That arrangement is valid which, whatever the matter, necessarily yields a conclusion once the premises are granted.

units.la: 337 Syllogismus contractus vel tertia figura dispositionem habet omnium simplicissimam, clarissimam & facillimam.
units.tr: The contracted syllogism, or third figure, has the simplest, clearest and easiest arrangement of all.

units.la: 338 In ista figura tertium argumentum antecedit, tum in propositione, tum in assumptione : assumptio est affirmativa, conclusio particularis.
units.tr: In this figure the middle term comes first, both in the major premise and in the minor. The minor is affirmative and the conclusion particular.

units.la: 339 Si particularis conclufio fit pluralis numeri, cùm fingularis tantùm fuit in præmiffis, tum fyllogifmus eft falfus.
units.tr: If the particular conclusion becomes plural when there was only a singular term in the premises, the syllogism is false.

units.la: 340 Expofitorius qui dicitur Syllogifmus, cujus tertium argumentum eft res fingularis, pertinet ad iftam figuram.
units.tr: The so-called expository syllogism, whose middle term is a singular thing, belongs to this figure.

units.la: 341 In explicato Syllogifmo, vel in prima & fecunda figura, propofitio nunquam debet effe particularis, conclufio eft particularis aut propria, fi ulla pars antecedens talis fuerit.
units.tr: In the explicit syllogism, that is, in the first and second figures, the major premise must never be particular. The conclusion is particular or proper if any antecedent part was of that kind.

units.la: 342 In primo explicato vel fecunda figura, tertium argumentum eft confequens pars propofitionis & affumptionis : conclufio femper negatur cum altera parte antecedentis.
units.tr: In the first explicit or second figure, the middle term is the consequent part of the major premise and of the minor. The conclusion is always denied together with the other part of the antecedent.

units.la: 343 In fecundo explicato vel prima figura tertium argumentum eft antecedens pars propofitionis, confequens affumptionis : affumptio hic femper affirmatur, vel formaliter, vel virtualiter.
units.tr: In the second explicit or first figure, the middle term is the antecedent part of the major premise and the consequent part of the minor. Here the minor is always affirmed, either formally or virtually.

units.la: 344 Syllogifmus compofitus non poteft femper revocari ad unum fimplicem.
units.tr: A compound syllogism cannot always be reduced to a simple one.

units.la: 345 In Syllogifmo compofito propofitio eft femper axioma compofitum & affirmatum.
units.tr: In a compound syllogism the major premise is always a compound axiom, and affirmed.

units.la: 346 Nullus Syllogifmus compofitus eft difcretus aut copulatus, fed tantùm connexus aut disjunctus.
units.tr: No compound syllogism is discrete or copulative; it is only connected or disjunctive.

units.la: 347 Axioma copulatum negatum vim habet axiomatis disjuncti ex parte, atque adeo ingreditur unum modum syllogismi disjuncti.
units.tr: A negated copulative axiom has the force, in part, of a disjunctive axiom, and so it enters into one mode of the disjunctive syllogism.

units.la: 348 Contradictio in Syllogismo compolito semper debet dividere verum à falso
units.tr: In a compound syllogism a contradiction must always separate the true from the false.

units.la: 349 In connexo Syllogismo nunquam assumitur consequens, aut tollitur antecedens in assumptione, sed vel assumitur antecedens, vel tollitur consequens: in conclusione nunquam concluditur antecedens, vel tollitur consequens.
units.tr: In a connected syllogism the consequent is never assumed, nor is the antecedent removed, in the minor premise. Rather, either the antecedent is assumed or the consequent is removed. In the conclusion, the antecedent is never concluded, nor is the consequent removed.

units.la: 350 In disjuncto Syllogismo assumitur vel tollitur altera pars disjunctionis.
units.tr: In a disjunctive syllogism one part of the disjunction is either assumed or removed.

units.la: 351 In disjuncto Syllogismo varii saepe termini unum constituunt argumentum.
units.tr: In a disjunctive syllogism several terms often make up one argument.

units.la: 352 Methodus est ars memoriae.
units.tr: Method is the art of memory.

units.la: 353 Methodus est proprie axiomatum, non argumentorum aut Syllogismorum; quia tamen axiomatum natura pendet ab argumentis, idcirco Methodus ab ipsis pendet.
units.tr: Method properly belongs to axioms, not to arguments or syllogisms. Yet, because the nature of axioms depends on arguments, method depends on them too.

units.la: 354 Methodus non magis est discursus quam axioma, sed Syllogismi discursus inservit utrique.
units.tr: Method is no more a discourse than an axiom is, but the discourse of the syllogism serves both.

units.la: 355 Homogeneitas, quae requiritur in methodo, non est partium axiomatis, quam lex καθ' αὑτὸ imperat, sed integrorum axiomatum, quae ad eandem finem & disciplinam debent spectare.
units.tr: The homogeneity required in method is not that of the parts of an axiom, which the law kath' hauto prescribes, but that of whole axioms, which ought to look to the same end and discipline.

units.la: 356 Ordo axiomatum sequitur ordinem rerum quem habent in natura sua.
units.tr: The order of axioms follows the order that things have in their own nature.

units.la: 357 In Methodo ἀϑεώρητα, non observatur ordo dignitatis, neque ordo existentiæ realis, sed ordo essentiæ & claritatis.
units.tr: In the method of athéoréta [ἀθεώρητα], the order of dignity is not observed, nor the order of real existence, but the order of essence and clarity.

units.la: 358 Quod clarius est & universalius illud debet præcedere.
units.tr: What is clearer and more universal ought to come first.

units.la: 359 Generalia generaliter & semel debent doceri.
units.tr: General matters should be taught generally and once only.

units.la: 360 Integrum definitur ante membrum, partim quia communius est, partim quia finis rationem habet, quò omnia membra referuntur.
units.tr: The whole is defined before the part, partly because it is more common, and partly because it serves as the end to which all the parts are referred.

units.la: 361 Methodus accurata est unica.
units.tr: An exact method is unique.

units.la: 362 Resolutio & compositio sunt quasi partes hujus methodi.
units.tr: Resolution and composition are, as it were, the parts of this method.

units.la: 363 Methodus prout accommodatur ad homines vel movendos, vel fallendos, vel delectandos, nullam certam habet regulam.
units.tr: Method, as it is adapted to moving, deceiving or delighting people, has no fixed rule.

units.la: 364 In oratione & similibus exercitiis duæ partes sunt necessariæ, propositio causæ & ejusdem confirmatio, cæteræ omnes sunt arbitrariæ, prout auditorum dispositio, & dicentis prudentia sese habeant.
units.tr: In a speech and similar exercises two parts are necessary: the statement of the case and its confirmation. All the rest is optional, depending on how the disposition of the hearers and the prudence of the speaker turn out.

units.la: FINIS
units.tr: THE END
